newsitem.title: FRANCE: OECD investment liberalisation accord delayed.
newsitem.headline: OECD investment liberalisation accord delayed.

text.p: Negotiators trying to hammer out a "treaty" to lift foreign investment restrictions across the 29 OECD countries said on Wednesday they would fail to meet a May deadline and were now aiming for the year end.

Frans Engering, chairman of talks on what would be the first legally binding pact among the club of industrialised countries, said an agreement was still too far away and would not be ready for OECD ministers to endorse at their annual May meeting.

"We have to recommend that the ministers give us a little more time," Engering told reporters at the headquarters of the Organisation of Economic Co-Operation and Development, where talks on the investment accord are taking place this week.

Engering played down the scale of the obstacles to a deal -- which the OECD hopes developing countries will sign up to as well. But he cited apparently fundamental areas on which a deal was still not in the making.

Above all, national representatives at the OECD have filed lists of "reservations" marking the areas they want excluded from the general liberalisation of investment, in domains such as air and water transport and energy.

"It's a bit unrealistic, having seen the list of reservations that have come in since February, to say that we could finish on time," Engering said, adding that talks could now need four or five months or even up to the end of the year.

He said negotiators were still toying with the kind of dispute settlement mechanisms that would be used and how to sanction those who fail to respect the agreement -- including the sensitive issue of whether to impose fines.

The delays could end up setting the pact back by a year, given that it would likely have to get the final stamp of approval at the ministerial-level gathering of OECD members, which takes place only once a year, each May.
